epic.title: Traceable Leave Approval Workflow
epic.description:
Replace the informal, email-based leave approval process with a system where every leave request reaches an explicit, recorded decision — enforcing HR sign-off for long or over-balance requests and producing a full audit trail.

**Business value:** Eliminates the recurring payroll surprise of unapproved leave and the compliance exposure of undocumented decisions; gives HR and the works council a defensible audit trail while keeping routine approvals fast.

**In scope:**
- Leave/Absence request lifecycle: submitted → manager review → HR review (mandatory above 10 days or over-balance) → approved/rejected
- Manager delegation to a named substitute for a date range
- 3-working-day stall detection and auto-escalation to HR
- Cancellation flow with automatic same-night balance restoration
- Nightly bidirectional sync with the legacy HR tool (balances, approvals, cancellations write-back)
- Mismatch handling: requests during an unresolved sync mismatch proceed flagged at-risk, never blocked
- Full audit trail (who approved/overrode/escalated/cancelled, when), retained 5 years
- Reporting-line-based permissions and HR override rights
- Single shared rule set for the pilot (no per-department/country configuration)

**Out of scope:**
- Per-department / per-country rule configuration
- Migrating balance ownership off the legacy HR tool (post-pilot decision)
- Generalizing the approval+delegation+escalation logic into a reusable cross-module circuit (noted as a future opportunity)
- Platform-level compliance/audit-trail service reused by other modules (future opportunity)
- Organizational enforcement against email-based approvals (policy/communication lever, not a build item)

issues.title: Resolve the zero-mismatch metric vs. nightly-sync design conflict
issues.description: The pilot's success bar of 'zero unresolved balance mismatches at month end' assumes a level of accuracy the nightly (not real-time) sync design doesn't guarantee. Decide with the client whether the metric should be reworded as 'resolved within 24h' or whether over-balance checks need a live call to the legacy tool, before this is baked into acceptance testing.

issues.title: Model the Leave/Absence request entity
issues.description: Build the Leave/Absence data model (employee, dates, duration, status, approver chain, balance reference, over-balance flag, at-risk flag). Field-level detail beyond what the workflow needs was inferred, not itemized by the client — confirm before finalizing the schema.

issues.title: Build the core request lifecycle state machine
issues.description: Implement states submitted → manager review → HR review → approved/rejected, with cancellation as a parallel transition. This is the backbone every other rule (HR sign-off, escalation, cancellation) plugs into.

issues.title: Implement manager approval and named-substitute delegation
issues.description: Manager approves by default following the reporting line; support delegating approval authority to a named substitute for a specific date range.

issues.title: Implement mandatory HR sign-off for long/over-balance requests
issues.description: Route to HR review whenever duration exceeds 10 working days or the request exceeds available balance; over-balance requests are allowed but must be flagged and cannot be manager-approved alone. Include HR override authority over any decision.

issues.title: Add stall detection and auto-escalation to HR
issues.description: If a request has no named backup approver and sits unresolved for 3 working days, auto-escalate it to HR so no request stalls silently.

issues.title: Implement cancellation with automatic balance restoration
issues.description: Allow cancellation while submitted, or up to 48h before start if already approved; restore balance automatically the same night without requiring HR confirmation.

issues.title: Build nightly bidirectional sync with the legacy HR tool
issues.description: Sync balances from the legacy tool (source of truth during the pilot) and write back approvals/cancellations the same night. Treat this as the pilot's dual-system dependency — an explicit post-pilot direction for balance ownership is still open.

issues.title: Handle balance mismatches without blocking requests
issues.description: When the nightly sync surfaces a disagreement, queue it for HR resolution the next morning; new requests submitted during that window proceed against the last-known balance and are flagged at-risk rather than blocked.

issues.title: Build the audit trail
issues.description: Log every approval, override, escalation and cancellation with actor and timestamp, retained 5 years for works-council compliance. Must cover at-risk and mismatch-window decisions, not just the happy path.

issues.title: Configure permissions for approval, override and delegation
issues.description: Approval rights follow the reporting line; HR can override any decision; a manager can delegate to a named substitute for a bounded date range. Verify these rules hold consistently across the manager and HR review states.

issues.title: Build audit trail reporting and export
issues.description: Provide a view/export of the audit trail sufficient for works-council and internal review, including turnaround time and mismatch/at-risk resolution tracking against the pilot's success metrics.

issues.title: Run end-to-end acceptance testing against pilot success criteria
issues.description: Validate: 100% of requests reach a recorded decision, no silent drops; mismatches resolved per the agreed metric wording; median turnaround under 2 working days; full manager adoption in-app; audit trail complete for a sample including at-risk and cancellation cases.

open_questions: What organizational lever (policy, payroll gate, HR spot-check) will ensure managers actually stop approving leave by email, since the workflow alone can't enforce that behavior change?

Is the legacy HR tool meant to remain the permanent balance source of truth after the pilot, or should balance ownership migrate into this platform — this shapes whether the nightly-sync/mismatch design is temporary or permanent?

Should the pilot's 'zero unresolved mismatches at month end' metric be reworded to match the async nightly-sync design (e.g. 'resolved within 24h'), or should over-balance checks call the legacy tool live instead?
